question: Do apparent-dark residual peaks occupy baryon-only vector-cancellation, incoherence, or tidal-saddle environments more often than same-radius control locations, and does one invariant transfer to held-out clusters and a second lens reconstruction?

field_motivation.candidate_activation: S_b=1-C or another frozen baryon-only invariant if it survives validation
field_motivation.interpretation: A stable low-coherence or saddle preference would identify where a baryon-sourced response might accumulate; it would not prove that gravity follows a path or that the standard convergence map is theory-neutral.

data.primary_peaks: P0567 Lenstool-ensemble positive residual peaks in ten fresh RELICS systems
data.spent_disclosure: The peak catalog and systems were inspected in P0567; the invariant definitions and gates are frozen before calculating their scores.

selection_and_validation.per_peak_score: midrank percentile of the real peak among 71 locations rotated by 5 through 355 degrees at the same cluster-centric radius
selection_and_validation.development_score: absolute equal-system mean of percentile minus 0.5; the development sign is frozen as high or low
selection_and_validation.multiple_search_control: 256 deterministic pseudo-peak trials choose one same-radius rotation per development system and record the largest absolute score across all 480 candidates
selection_and_validation.validation_score: development-signed equal-system mean centered percentile on the three different validation systems
selection_and_validation.method_score: development-signed equal-system centered percentile for independently reconstructed GLAFIC peaks
selection_and_validation.forward_rule: Run a separately frozen forward activation test only if every advance gate passes.

cross_domain.isolated_source: For a centered point source, vector cancellation, radial misalignment, and transverse fraction are exactly zero.
cross_domain.axisymmetric_galaxy: When bound baryonic components are represented by their net axisymmetric fields, those three invariants are exactly zero; this is an angular activation audit, not a standalone galaxy rotation law.
cross_domain.solar: The centered point-source limit is exactly zero and therefore adds no Solar force.

claim_limits: The apparent-dark peaks come from standard-GR parametric convergence reconstructions, not direct dark-matter detections or raw lensing observables.
The baryon proxy contains photometric member light but omits hot gas, intracluster light, and mass-to-light variation.
Member-level vector coherence depends on the chosen physical coarse-graining; it is not defined by microscopic particles.
Same-radius rotations control cluster-centric radius but do not reproduce every selection effect of peak finding.
Twenty-five primary peaks across ten systems provide limited validation power.
A correlation identifies a possible activation coordinate, not a gravity field equation or an explanation of galaxy rotation.
